subject: Access & Erasure request + DPIA / SCCs evidence request — Aurelia Health
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <privacy@aureliahealth.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-22 08:15:00 +0000
Subject: Data subject request — access + erasure; DPIA and SCCs evidence request

Hi Lauren,

Aurelia Health has received a formal data subject request from a patient who is requesting a copy of all personal data we processed via Redwood Inference and a subsequent deletion of that data. The request references Article 15 and 17 GDPR.

We also need to collect Redwood’s evidence for our DPIA and cross-border transfer controls (SCCs). Specifically:
- Confirmation of controller vs. processor role for our hosted API usage.
- Steps and expected timeline to export any records tied to a customer-provided ID and to carry out secure deletion.
- Copies of SCC annex text you rely on and a DPIA template or checklist you recommend we use.
- Any SOC 2 / SIG / CAIQ artifacts that show data flows and retention (redacted where necessary).

Attached is the signed DSR and the patient’s identifier (hashed on our side). We ask for an acknowledgement and a written plan for handling export + deletion within 3 business days.

Attachments: [aurelia_dsr_signed.pdf]

Thanks,
Elena Rossi
DPO Office — Aurelia Health
privacy@aureliahealth.com

-----
Note: please treat this request as time-sensitive and share the scope (which environments, e.g., hosted vs private) you will apply the actions to.

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <privacy@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-22 10:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Data subject request — access + erasure; DPIA and SCCs evidence request

Hi Elena — thanks for sending this over and for the clear scope. Acknowledged.

Quick summary of our position (so we’re explicit):
- For hosted API usage, Aurelia Health is the controller and Redwood Inference acts as a processor. For Private (customer-managed) deployments we can discuss different roles/arrangements.
- We can produce a data export for the identifier you provided and run a deletion workflow. Our standard processor timeline is to deliver an export and deletion confirmation within 30 calendar days of a validated request; we will prioritize since you flagged it as time-sensitive.

Next steps I’ll take immediately:
1) Validate the signed DSR and scope (I have the attached document).
2) Kick off an ops export job and a separate verified deletion workflow (I will copy ops).
3) Share the SCC annex we use plus DPIA checklist and our SOC 2 / SIG summary.

To proceed, can you confirm: (a) the specific customer account ID(s) impacted, (b) whether the request covers historical logs and raw request payloads stored in retention caches, and (c) who should receive the export (email or secure link)?

Attaching the privacy-process-checklist for our standard flow. I’ll loop in Legal and Ops for the export/deletion run.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: privacy-process-checklist.pdf]

Questions for Legal/Ops:
- Priyom: confirm we are processor only for Aurelia’s hosted usage and the exact deletion/export scope (do we include logs and persisted caches?), and whether we need an escalation to Privacy Counsel for cross-border DPIA support.
- Marcus: can Ops run the export + scoped deletion job and provide a verifiable deletion log? If so, estimated ETA.
- Monica: any account-specific details (account ID mapping) you can share from Customer Success?

I attached an internal-evidence-request.txt with the evidence Aurelia listed. Please reply with who will own each bullet and a short ETA; Elena asked for acknowledgement within 3 business days.

Thanks — Lauren

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-22 14:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: FW: Data subject request — access + erasure; DPIA and SCCs evidence request

Lauren / team — quick legal read and proposed plan:  

1) Role confirmation: for Aurelia’s hosted API usage we are a processor; customer remains controller. We should state this formally to the DPO.

2) Export & deletion scope: we will include customer-submitted payloads and model outputs tied to the provided identifier. We typically do not include ephemeral runtime logs (aggregated telemetry) unless the customer requests them specifically — however request asked about logs, so confirm with Aurelia if they want those.

3) Timeline: Ops to provide export within 5 business days and run deletion job within the same window; final deletion confirmation and a signed deletion log within 10 business days. If Aurelia needs a compressed timeline we can escalate.

4) Evidence artifacts: I’m attaching the SCCs annex we use, a DPIA template, and a SIG/SOC2 summary we can share (redacted). We will not disclose internal-only runbooks. For CAIQ/SIG full responses we can provide the customer-facing exported questionnaire PDF.

5) Cross-border note: SCCs are applicable for transfers outside the EEA; Marcus / Ops should confirm physical regions where data resides so we can populate the SCC annex properly.

Attachments I’ll circulate: sccs-annex.docx, dpia-template.docx, sig_responses_summary.pdf.

Priyom
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: sccs-annex.docx] [Attachment: dpia-template.docx] [Attachment: sig_responses_summary.pdf]

We also confirm we need the SCC annex populated with Redwood’s processing locations and the DPIA checklist to complete our internal assessment. SOC2 / SIG summary is sufficient for now — we will ask for more if needed.

Elena
